LESSON: The bbox+ST_Intersects(district_geom, county_geom) 'final guard' pattern (p2-juris-store.mjs HOIST_CITIES_SQL, parcel-school-district.mjs's old HOIST_SCHOOL_DISTRICTS_SQL, parcel-overlay-districts.mjs) is unsafe for any polygon layer whose real-world edges can run along a county line -- independently-digitized boundary datasets do not align to the meter (measured gap: 0.79-0.92m on this rail's data). Confirmed unsafe for tx_school_district (13 real parcels, 3 counties). The fix that worked here (drop the exact-intersects guard, keep bbox only, rely on the exact per-parcel test to decide correctness) generalizes as a DIAGNOSTIC METHOD, not as a blanket instruction to remove the guard everywhere: the falsifier is 'does an unscoped statewide ST_Contains find a real hit the per-county hoist misses', and it must be re-run on each rail's own live data before touching that rail's hoist.

When a lane's own leading hypothesis (mechanism A, degenerate geometry) has 'heavy prior art', test it against the specific parcels named, not against the prior-art pattern in general -- these 13 shared none of the cited prior-art shapes (prop_id collisions, literal-string prop_ids, StratMap grafts) despite superficially resembling that class (small, round number, blocking a publish gate).
DEAD-END: Initially mis-read p2-juris-store.mjs's HOIST_CITIES_SQL as bbox-only (grep -A40 truncated before the final WHERE clause) and nearly justified the fix as 'matching the city pattern'. Re-reading the full file showed cities carry the identical ST_Intersects guard. The fix's real justification is narrower and correct (this guard is specifically wrong for a polygon layer whose real edges run along county lines), not 'cities already do it this way'.
